checks.result: capture chooses fixed tempfile.gettempdir()/jarvis_screenshots, accepts an existing directory at screenshot.py24-25, builds a second-resolution basename at27-28 and delegates pathname opening to mss.tools.to_png at32. There is no owner/mode/symlink/exclusive-create check or retained directory/file descriptor. VisionClient subsequently reopens the returned path for read_bytes at vision.py104-105. Parent-supplied static upstream MSS9.0.1 writer observation corroborates ordinary pathname opening, but no installed dependency or capture behavior was executed here.

Neither inspected desktop source nor container definitions establishes the effective user temporary root, umask, private-temp isolation or another UID ability to precreate/populate the namespace. candidates.title: Shared temporary screenshot namespace may redirect capture output across OS users
candidates.description: Capture trusts an existing fixed jarvis_screenshots directory under the effective temporary root and uses a predictable second-resolution PNG name. If a different OS principal can precreate or populate that namespace and the installed PNG writer follows existing paths, one later victim capture may disclose synthetic screen bytes through an attacker-controlled output or overwrite a victim-writable dummy file. Source establishes the path trust gap, but private temporary roots, dependency availability and OS permissions can prevent this result. No capture, separate-UID effect, disclosure or overwrite was demonstrated. Native voice and vision callers make the boundary independent of the separate stock HTTP Authority admission limitation.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: Generated screenshot storage trusts attacker-influenceable directory and leaf path state without owner/mode validation or descriptor-bound exclusive publication.

trace.description: The default fixed temporary namespace is selected; mkdir(exist_ok=True) accepts preexisting filesystem state without determining which OS principal owns it.
The output basename depends on the capture second, and an absolute pathname is constructed without opening or pinning its directory or leaf.
Synthetic or real captured RGB bytes are passed to the installed mss.tools.to_png writer with that pathname as output; the application adds no no-follow or exclusive-create control.

evidence.description: mss is imported before directory selection or hardware capture; absence prevents this path from executing.
Temporary root selection is runtime-dependent, and the fixed child directory receives no ownership, permissions or symlink validation.
The second-resolution output name is predictable and no verified output descriptor is created by the application.
The installed PNG writer receives a pathname rather than a retained verified descriptor.
The normal execute wrapper refuses real capture in global dry-run mode.
Strict approval mode requires confirmation even for the Level0 screenshot tool; normal registry dry-run also gates execution.
Ordinary screenshot chat requests construct only monitor parameters; they do not expose arbitrary output_dir input.
Native voice routes transcripts through the tool-processing helpers directly, without depending exclusively on HTTP application lifespan.
Screen analysis calls the same capture helper; its later file read at104-105 is pathname-based.
Desktop installation declares mss>=9.0.0, which does not establish the exact installed writer implementation or an operational desktop.
The existing capture test replaces the PNG writer with a mock; it cannot establish real writer behavior, cross-UID permissions or shared-temp effects.

validation_plan.local: Use a separately approved OS-isolated disposable fixture with two dummy UIDs, a synthetic shared temporary root, and an already available approved mss dependency. Mock only pixel acquisition and use the real PNG writer. Predeclare one harmless output and one victim-owned dummy file; allow the lower-trust UID to set up only the synthetic namespace, then invoke one capture as the victim and stop after observing rejection, redirected synthetic bytes or dummy-file overwrite. Compare a victim-owned0700 private-root control. Record effective directory/file modes, applicable OS link protections and writer version. Never access a real desktop, host temporary root, production file or credential, and do not fetch/install dependencies during this audit.
validation_plan.deployment: Ask the owner to inspect capture enablement, installed mss version, effective TMPDIR/TEMP or per-user temp directory, directory/ancestor ownership and ACLs, umask and private-temp isolation without displaying screenshots or credentials. Determine whether a different local UID can precreate/populate the generated namespace. No production capture or service probing is requested.

hardening: For screenshot.py17-35, create unpredictable victim-owned0700 per-capture storage under a verified private root and create the PNG file exclusively with0600/O_NOFOLLOW using a pinned directory descriptor. Obtain PNG bytes from mss.tools.to_png(output=None) and write through that descriptor rather than letting the dependency reopen an absolute path; consume the same verified bytes/descriptor in vision and verifier paths.

Add regression coverage for preexisting foreign-owned directories, directory and leaf symlinks, timestamp collisions and private-root preventing controls. Existing mocked writer tests do not qualify different-UID filesystem isolation.

Do not classify the trusted explicit output_dir library parameter as an unauthenticated HTTP write primitive: ordinary chat construction supplies only monitor. No installed/deployed screenshot exploit or severity is asserted.
